candidateEvidence.excerpt: NVIDIA announced on September 3 that it has agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $12.93 billion. It says the deal will help it strengthen and expand the platform. This is an announced agreement; we have not verified that the purchase has closed.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: NVIDIA has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12,930,300,000. Together, we will scale Hugging Face’s platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide. Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem. Developers will choose the models they want, the frameworks they want, the clouds and inference service providers they want and the computing platforms they want. NVIDIA compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.

scopeAndFreshness: P002 matches the NVIDIA announcement passage: agreement, September 3, $12,930,300,000 rounded to $12.93 billion, strengthen/expand framing, and the article correctly states closing is unverified.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: NVIDIA builds chips, computer systems and AI software. Hugging Face gives people a place to find and share trained AI models—the parts of AI tools that process input to produce a result. Builders can download models from its Hub or connect to services that run them. The catalogue and the computing are different parts of getting AI into a tool someone can use.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: NVIDIA engineers the most advanced chips, systems, and software for the AI factories of the future.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Why the name? It comes from the hugging-face emoji, 🤗. Co-founder Clem Delangue says the founders expected to keep the name for only a few weeks or months. Then their community embraced it—on social posts, T-shirts and other merchandise—and they decided it had to stay.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: At the beginning, we thought we would keep the name maybe for a few weeks, for a few months, but then the community started to use it everywhere and to put it on social networks when we were posting things, to add it to their T-shirts or to other swag ... there's no way we're going to change this. We need to keep it.

scopeAndFreshness: P005 matches Delangue's quoted account: expected the name for weeks or months, community adoption on social posts and T-shirts, decision to keep it.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Why does Hugging Face sound familiar? You may have seen it in reports about OpenAI’s experimental AI agents. OpenAI says that, during internal security tests in July, models operating with reduced safeguards bypassed restrictions meant to keep them isolated from the internet and gained unauthorized access to Hugging Face’s systems. That was a testing security failure, rather than ordinary ChatGPT use, and it is separate from this acquisition announcement. Read OpenAI’s account of the incident.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The incident occurred during cybersecurity evaluations of several OpenAI models ... The models, operating under reduced safeguards, took actions that were misaligned with the goals of their assigned tasks—they communicated through unauthorized channels, exploited vulnerabilities in shared infrastructure, gained internet access, and accessed third-party systems. ... On July 10, an agent located publicly exposed Hugging Face user credentials ... Later, an agent used these credentials to discover and chain together several security exploits that gave it full code execution capabilities on several Hugging Face servers.

scopeAndFreshness: P007 accurately attributes to OpenAI the July testing incident under reduced safeguards, including unauthorized access to Hugging Face systems, and correctly separates it from ordinary use and from the acquisition.
